authorities.title: Right to a State Fair Hearing
authorities.summary: A Medi-Cal member who disagrees with a county or state action may request a State Hearing within 90 days of receiving the Notice of Action. Late requests may be accepted with good cause, such as illness or disability.
authorities.how_to_use: Use the Request for State Hearing on the back of the notice, mail or fax it to CDSS State Hearings Division (fax 833-281-0905), file online, or call 1-800-743-8525. Keep a dated copy.

authorities.title: Keeping Coverage During a Hearing (Aid Paid Pending)
authorities.summary: Coverage continues unchanged while a hearing is pending if the member requests the hearing before the effective date of the action when ten-day advance notice is required, or within 10 days of the notice date when it is not.
authorities.how_to_use: Request the hearing before the effective date printed on the notice and write "I request aid paid pending" on the request.

authorities.title: Ten-Day Advance Notice Before Adverse Action
authorities.summary: A Medicaid agency must mail a notice at least 10 days before the date of an action that terminates, suspends, or reduces eligibility or covered services, with limited exceptions.
authorities.how_to_use: If the effective date is less than 10 days after the notice date, flag the notice as possibly defective and raise it in the hearing request.

authorities.title: Required Contents of a Notice of Action
authorities.summary: A notice of adverse action must state the action, the clear reasons for it, the specific regulations that support it, the right to request a hearing, and the circumstances under which coverage continues if a hearing is requested.
authorities.how_to_use: If a notice gives no specific reason or no supporting regulation, flag it as possibly inadequate and raise it in the hearing request.

authorities.title: Renewals, Requests for Information, and the 90-Day Reconsideration Period
authorities.summary: The agency must first try to renew coverage using information it already has. If it needs more, it must give the member at least 30 days to return the renewal form or requested information. If coverage ends for failure to return the form, the member can return it within 90 days after termination to have eligibility reconsidered without a new application.
authorities.how_to_use: Return documents before the due date and keep proof of submission. If coverage already ended for a missing form, return it within the 90-day window.

authorities.title: Medicaid Community Engagement (Work Reporting) Requirement
authorities.summary: Beginning January 1, 2027, Medicaid expansion adults ages 19 to 64 must show 80 hours per month of work, community service, job training, or at least half-time school (or a combination), or monthly income of at least 80 times the federal minimum wage (about $580), unless an exemption applies.
authorities.how_to_use: First screen for exemptions. If none applies, gather pay stubs, school enrollment, or volunteer verification for the month the notice names.

authorities.title: Exemptions From the Community Engagement Requirement
authorities.summary: People exempt from the requirement include those who are pregnant or within the postpartum period, parents and caregivers of a child age 13 or younger, people with a disability or who are medically frail (including serious or complex medical conditions and substance use disorder), recently incarcerated individuals within 90 days of release, American Indians and Alaska Natives, veterans with a total disability rating, and people already meeting SNAP or TANF work requirements.
authorities.how_to_use: If any exemption applies, respond to the notice by stating the exemption and attaching proof, such as a birth record, a child's birth certificate, or a clinician's statement.

authorities.title: 30-Day Period to Respond to a Noncompliance Notice
authorities.summary: Before ending coverage for not meeting the requirement, the state must send a noncompliance notice and give the member 30 days to show compliance or an exemption. Coverage continues during those 30 days, and the state must consider every other basis for eligibility before ending coverage.
authorities.how_to_use: Respond within 30 days of the notice date with proof of hours or proof of an exemption. Keep a dated copy.

authorities.title: Six-Month Renewals for Expansion Adults
authorities.summary: Medicaid expansion adults will renew eligibility every six months instead of every twelve months. California has announced an effective date in early 2027.
authorities.how_to_use: Calendar the next renewal six months out and keep income documents current.

authorities.title: 12 Months of Postpartum Coverage
authorities.summary: Medi-Cal continues full coverage for 12 months after pregnancy ends for eligible members, including postpartum checkups, mental health care, and prescriptions.
authorities.how_to_use: If a postpartum member receives a termination notice within 12 months of the end of pregnancy, raise postpartum continuous coverage in the response or hearing request.

authorities.title: Pregnancy Coverage and Presumptive Eligibility
authorities.summary: Pregnant people can receive immediate, temporary Medi-Cal coverage for prenatal care through presumptive eligibility at a qualified provider while a full application is processed.
authorities.how_to_use: If prenatal care is at risk because of a coverage gap, ask a qualified prenatal provider about presumptive eligibility the same day.

authorities.title: Emergency Care Regardless of Coverage
authorities.summary: Hospitals with emergency departments that participate in Medicare must screen and stabilize anyone with an emergency condition, including active labor, regardless of insurance or ability to pay.
authorities.how_to_use: Remind the client that a coverage gap never prevents emergency screening and stabilization.

authorities.title: Women's Preventive Services at No Cost
authorities.summary: Most health plans must cover HRSA-supported women's preventive services without cost sharing, including well-woman visits, contraception, breastfeeding support and pumps, and screening for postpartum depression and interpersonal violence.
authorities.how_to_use: Remind the client which preventive visits to keep scheduled while coverage questions are resolved.

authorities.title: Right to Free Language Assistance
authorities.summary: People with limited English proficiency have the right to free interpreters and translated materials from health programs and state agencies. Medi-Cal provides notices and help in threshold languages, which include Tagalog and Spanish in many counties.
authorities.how_to_use: If the client reads Tagalog, Spanish, or another language, request the notice and future notices in that language and an interpreter for any interview or hearing.

authorities.title: Discrimination Complaints to DHCS Office of Civil Rights
authorities.summary: A member who believes Medi-Cal treated them unfairly because of sex, language, disability, or another protected trait may file a civil rights complaint with the DHCS Office of Civil Rights within 180 days of the last act.
authorities.how_to_use: File by phone, mail, or email with the DHCS Office of Civil Rights and keep a copy.
